extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of long-time behavior and geometric decomposition for Ricci flow with surgery on compact orientable three-manifolds, including curvature/volume criteria, thick-thin decomposition, and conclusions about persistent hyperbolic pieces or collapse to graph manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of V(t)(t + 3/2)^{-3/2}
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the cutoff surgeries do not increase volume, d/dt log V(t) - (3/2) log(t + 3/2) ≤ 0 for all t ≥ 0. Equivalently, the function V(t) (t + 3/2)^{-3/2} is nonincreasing on [0, ∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to control total volume and to obtain inequalities such as (7.6.4); the inequality is derived by noting surgeries do not increase volume and integrating curvature-related terms (see (7.6.3) and (7.6.4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.1 (limit of rescalings has constant sectional curvature)
rubrics_metrics.description: If gij(t) is a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery and for a fixed 0 < r < 1 and times t_α → ∞ the rescalings of the solution on the parabolic neighborhoods P(x_α, t_α, r√t_α, r^2 t_α) with factor (t_α)^{-1} and time-shifted to 1 converge in the C^∞ topology to some smooth limiting solution on an abstract parabolic neighborhood P( x̄, 1, r, 1/4 ), then the limiting solution has constant sectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compactness/limit criterion (via parabolic rescaling and Hamilton compactness) is the bridge from local curvature/volume control to concluding asymptotic homogeneity (constant curvature) of limits; employed to deduce asymptotic curvature results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2 (Perelman) — local curvature closeness (i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ε > 0, for any w > 0, r > 0, ξ > 0 one can find T = T(w,r,ξ,ε) < ∞ such that: if the geodesic ball B_{t0}(x0, r√t0) at some time t0 ≥ T has volume at least w (r√t0)^3 and the sectional curvature bounded below appropriately (as in the statement), then the quantity |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| at (x0, t0) is < ξ (inequality (7.6.5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: T depends on w,r,ξ,ε. The proof combines volume comparison, Theorem 7.5.2 (curvature control under volume lower bound), curvature pinching and Lemma 7.6.1 to convert local volume and lower-curvature bounds into smallness of the normalized Ricci tensor 2tR_{ij}+g_{ij} at the center point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2 (Perelman) — uniform curvature closeness on spatial balls (ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the same hypotheses as (i) and given in addition A < ∞, by allowing T = T(w,r,ξ,A,ε) one can ensure the estimate |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| < ξ holds for all points in the spatial ball B_{t0}(x0, A r√t0) (inequality (7.6.5) uniformly on the ball).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To upgrade the pointwise estimate to a ball one must get an upper bound for scalar curvature on a larger parabolic neighborhood and use canonical neighborhood results and volume/curvature estimates; constants K1,K2,K'1 etc depend on w,r,A,ε.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2 (Perelman) — forward parabolic neighborhood estimate (iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the same hypotheses and with A < ∞, the estimate |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| < ξ holds on the forward parabolic neighborhood P(x0, t0, A r√t0, A r^2 t0) (i.e., spatial ball of radius Ar√t0 and forward time interval of length Ar^2 t0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends spatial control to a spacetime neighborhood by combining the time-evolution of length/volume with the prior curvature and volume bounds and by ruling out surgeries or blowups in the controlled region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (ε-necks and ε-caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Points with sufficiently large scalar curvature (above specified thresholds depending on parameters) have canonical neighborhoods: they are either ε-necks or ε-caps satisfying specified curvature and geometric bounds (scalar curvature comparable in the neighborhood, size scales controlled by R^{-1/2}, volume and geometry estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption provides local geometric models used repeatedly to obtain volume and curvature estimates (e.g., to find constants c1,C2 and to argue existence of canonical neighborhoods on balls where scalar curvature is above certain thresholds). It is used to derive estimates like (7.6.9)-(7.6.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local curvature bounds on parabolic neighborhoods (estimates (7.6.7), (7.6.11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the volume and curvature lower bounds one obtains concrete curvature estimates of the form |Rm| ≤ K'(r0√t0)^{-2} on P(x0,t0,r0√t0, -τ(r0√t0)^2) (7.6.7), and similarly |Rm| ≤ K'1(r√t0)^{-2} on spatial balls B_{t0}(x0, 2A r√t0) (7.6.11), where the constants depend only on parameters w,r,A,ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These quantitative bounds are intermediate steps used to apply compactness theorems and Lemma 7.6.1; the constants K',K'1,K1,K2 etc are produced by Theorems 7.5.1/7.5.2 together with the pinching assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thick–thin decomposition theorem (Theorem 7.6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w > 0 and small ε > 0 there exists ρ = ρ(w,ε) > 0 so that for sufficiently large t the manifold M_t decomposes as M_thin(w,t) ∪ M_thick(w,t) with: (a) for x ∈ M_thin there exists r = r(x,t) with 0 < r√t < ρ√t such that Rm ≥ −(r√t)^{-2} on B_t(x,r√t) and Vol_t(B_t(x,r√t)) < w (r√t)^3; (b) for x ∈ M_thick we have |2t R_{ij} + g_{ij}| < ξ on B_t(x, ρ√t) and Vol_t(B_t(x, ρ√t)) ≥ (1/10) w (ρ√t)^3. Moreover, suitable scalings of points in the thick part converge to complete hyperbolic manifolds of finite volume with constant sectional curvature (as in the statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem gives a geometric partition into collapsed (thin) regions with local negative curvature lower bound and small volume, and thick regions close to hyperbolic geometry; constants ρ, ξ, and the dependence on ε are explicit in the construction. The convergence statement provides the hyperbolic limit models for the thick part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-time behavior theorem for Ricci flow with surgery (Theorem 7.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given small parameters w, ε and a solution (M_t,gij(t)) of Ricci flow with surgery with normalized initial data and nonincreasing functions r(t), δ(t), one of three alternatives holds for large time: (i) eventually M_t = M_thin(w,t) for all large t; or (ii) there exists a sequence t_α → ∞ so that scalings of g_{ij}(t_α) on the essential component converge in C^∞ to a hyperbolic metric on the initial compact manifold M; or (iii) there is a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds of finite volume and truncated compact subsets K_l (by small-area constant mean curvature tori), and for large t diffeomorphisms φ_l embed these truncated pieces into M_t so that t^{-1} φ_l^*(g_{ij}(t)) is arbitrarily close to the hyperbolic metric on each K_l, the union of these images lies in the thick part and their complements lie in the thin part, and the boundary tori are incompressible (inject π1 of torus into π1(M_t)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem summarizes the possible geometric ends: pure collapse, global convergence to a hyperbolic metric, or finitely many persistent hyperbolic pieces plus thin complements. The result depends on the canonical neighborhood structure, volume monotonicity, and the thick–thin decomposition; incompressibility of boundary tori is shown via minimal-disk/area-decrease arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman’s Claim / Shioya–Yamaguchi weaker assertion (collapse ⇒ graph manifold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman’s asserted claim: For a sequence of compact orientable three-manifolds (possibly with convex boundary) with parameters w_α → 0, if for each point x there is a radius ρ = ρ_α(x) ≤ diam(M_α) so that the ball B(x,ρ) has volume at most w_α ρ^3 and sectional curvatures at least −ρ^{-2}, and boundary components (if any) have small diameter and appropriate collars, then for sufficiently large α the manifolds M_α are diffeomorphic to graph manifolds. Shioya–Yamaguchi proved the weaker assertion for the closed (no-boundary) case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the topological conclusion corresponding to local metric collapse with a two-sided (lower) curvature bound: local collapse forces graph-manifold topology. The full Perelman claim includes boundary/collar conditions; the closed case suffices for many geometrization arguments (as referenced in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompressibility of boundary tori by minimal-disk area decrease
rubrics_metrics.description: If a boundary torus T of a persistent hyperbolic piece were compressible into the complement, there's a least-area embedded disk D in the complement with ∂D ⊂ T. Under the normalized metric g̃_{ij}(t) = t^{-1} g_{ij}(t) the area A(t) of this minimal disk satisfies a differential inequality (7.6.21)-(7.6.22) of the form dA/dt ≤ −(π/t) + o(1) (more precisely negative and not integrable), which leads to a contradiction for large t; hence the boundary tori are incompressible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument uses evolution of area under the normalized Ricci flow, Gauss-Bonnet, estimates on Ricci and scalar curvature in the hyperbolic piece (surgeries do not affect the piece), and replacement/compactness arguments to handle possible surgeries crossing the disk. This is the key geometric-topological criterion proving incompressibility.
